biggest_gap.title: A yes/no custom field with a default breaks saving contacts: import crashes with a 500, API creates are refused, and once the field is required no existing contact can be saved from its form
biggest_gap.detail: The spec lets an administrator give any field a default. For a yes/no field, a default stops other saves from working. CustomFieldService.SaveAsync applies a missing field's default as JsonSerializer.SerializeToElement(field.Default), which gives the JSON string "true". ParseAsync for a boolean accepts only JSON true or false, so the default it applies itself is refused as customFieldBoolean. This breaks three things. (1) Every contact created through the API without that key is refused: 400 on customFields.<key>, 'Choose yes or no.', for a field the caller never sent. (2) Every contact import is affected. The dry run reports the rows as valid, then the real run answers 500, InvalidOperationException 'A custom field value that passed the check was refused on saving'. Nothing is imported. (3) Mark the field required and every existing contact (100,007 in the demo) is affected. Saving one unchanged from its form shows 'Choose yes or no.' under a select that already shows Yes; in Arabic, 'اختر نعم أو لا.' under نعم. This round's fix for 'required field with a default' works for text, number, date and select, but goes through the same default path and so misses yes/no. Only the new-contact form works, because it sends true itself. For a UAE trader, a 'VAT registered: Yes' or 'Key account' flag with a default is a common first custom field. Adding it would stop imports and block edits of old customers, while Odoo applies a boolean field's default without trouble. The fix: build the default from the field's type (JsonOfText already does this for booleans) before parsing, and add a test for each type × {new via API, import, old record required}. This is not a release blocker in itself: the round is BLOCKED because no clean-clone verify passed (see hard_gates; not p09's code).
